BOOK_INTROS.Genesis: The book of beginnings, creation, the first families, the call of Abraham, and the journey of Joseph into Egypt.
BOOK_INTROS.Exodus: Moses leads Israel out of slavery in Egypt, receives the Ten Commandments, and the people learn to live as a nation under God.
BOOK_INTROS.Leviticus: A handbook of worship, ritual, and daily holiness for the priests and people of ancient Israel.
BOOK_INTROS.Numbers: Israel's forty-year journey through the wilderness, told through censuses, complaints, victories, and divine guidance.
BOOK_INTROS.Deuteronomy: Moses' farewell sermons to a new generation about to enter the Promised Land, restating the covenant in plainer words.
BOOK_INTROS.Joshua: The conquest and settlement of Canaan under Joshua, Moses' successor, and the dividing of the land among the twelve tribes.
BOOK_INTROS.Judges: Twelve cycles of crisis and rescue as Israel drifts from God and is rescued by judges like Deborah, Gideon, and Samson.
BOOK_INTROS.Ruth: A short story of loyalty and providence: a Moabite widow's faithfulness becomes the line that leads to King David.
BOOK_INTROS.1 Samuel: The transition from judges to kings, with the rise of Samuel, the failure of Saul, and the anointing of David.
BOOK_INTROS.2 Samuel: The reign of King David, told without flattery: his triumphs, his great sin, and the consequences that follow.
BOOK_INTROS.1 Kings: Solomon builds the Temple in Jerusalem, but the kingdom splits in two and prophets like Elijah challenge the kings.
BOOK_INTROS.2 Kings: The slow decline and exile of both kingdoms, punctuated by the ministries of Elisha and the reformer kings.
BOOK_INTROS.1 Chronicles: Israel's history retold from a priestly perspective, beginning with genealogies and centering on David's preparations for the Temple.
BOOK_INTROS.2 Chronicles: The story of Judah's kings, from Solomon to the exile, with particular attention to faithful and unfaithful worship.
BOOK_INTROS.Ezra: The return from Babylonian exile and the rebuilding of the Temple in Jerusalem.
BOOK_INTROS.Nehemiah: The rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls and the spiritual renewal of the returned community.
BOOK_INTROS.Esther: A Jewish queen in Persia risks her life to save her people from genocide. The book never names God but shows His hand throughout.
BOOK_INTROS.Job: An honest, ancient wrestling with the question of why good people suffer.
BOOK_INTROS.Psalms: One hundred and fifty songs and prayers covering the full range of human experience before God: praise, grief, anger, trust, longing.
BOOK_INTROS.Proverbs: A collection of practical wisdom for everyday life, drawn largely from Solomon and other sages.
BOOK_INTROS.Ecclesiastes: An older voice reflects on the limits of human wisdom and the meaning of work, pleasure, and time.
BOOK_INTROS.Song of Solomon: A series of love poems celebrating romantic and physical love, read by Christians and Jews alike as also pointing toward divine love.
BOOK_INTROS.Isaiah: Sweeping prophecies of judgment and hope, including some of the most cited messianic passages in the Bible.
BOOK_INTROS.Jeremiah: The 'weeping prophet' speaks God's word during the fall of Jerusalem, mourning a people who would not listen.
BOOK_INTROS.Lamentations: Five poems of grief over the destruction of Jerusalem.
BOOK_INTROS.Ezekiel: Visions and parables from a prophet in exile, including the valley of dry bones and the new Temple.
BOOK_INTROS.Daniel: Stories of faithfulness in exile (the lions' den, the fiery furnace) paired with visions of empires rising and falling.
BOOK_INTROS.Hosea: A prophet whose troubled marriage becomes a living parable of God's love for an unfaithful people.
BOOK_INTROS.Joel: A prophecy occasioned by a locust plague, with a vision of God's Spirit poured out on all flesh.
BOOK_INTROS.Amos: A shepherd from Tekoa speaks blunt words about justice, the poor, and empty religion.
BOOK_INTROS.Obadiah: The shortest book in the Old Testament, addressed to the people of Edom.
BOOK_INTROS.Jonah: A reluctant prophet, a great fish, and the discovery that God's mercy reaches even to enemies.
BOOK_INTROS.Micah: A contemporary of Isaiah who speaks of judgment and of a coming ruler from Bethlehem.
BOOK_INTROS.Nahum: A prophecy concerning the fall of Nineveh.
BOOK_INTROS.Habakkuk: A prophet's honest dialogue with God about the problem of evil.
BOOK_INTROS.Zephaniah: A prophecy of the day of the Lord, ending in restoration.
BOOK_INTROS.Haggai: A short book urging the returned exiles to finish rebuilding the Temple.
BOOK_INTROS.Zechariah: Visions and prophecies encouraging the rebuilding of the Temple and looking forward to a coming king.
BOOK_INTROS.Malachi: The last voice of the Old Testament prophets, calling for renewal before the day of the Lord.
BOOK_INTROS.1 Esdras: An alternative Greek account of events from the late Old Testament period, retelling parts of Chronicles, Ezra, and Nehemiah with additional material including the famous contest of the three young guardsmen.
BOOK_INTROS.2 Esdras: A Jewish apocalyptic work in seven visions, wrestling with the destruction of Jerusalem and the problem of evil. Sometimes called 4 Ezra.
BOOK_INTROS.Tobit: A short, vivid story of two faithful Israelites in exile, an angel in disguise, a fish that yields medicine, and a marriage that breaks a curse.
BOOK_INTROS.Judith: A widow of remarkable courage saves her people by going into the camp of an invading general. A story of faith, fasting, and one decisive moment.
BOOK_INTROS.Esther (Greek): Six additional passages found in the Greek text of Esther but not the Hebrew, including prayers by Mordecai and Esther and the texts of royal decrees. Following the 1611 King James arrangement, these passages are numbered as chapters 10 through 16, beginning where the canonical Hebrew Esther ends.
BOOK_INTROS.Wisdom of Solomon: A philosophical meditation in the voice of Solomon, on wisdom, righteousness, immortality, and the folly of idolatry.
BOOK_INTROS.Sirach: Also called Ecclesiasticus. A long collection of practical wisdom from a Jerusalem teacher named Jesus ben Sirach, around 180 BC. Read widely in synagogues and churches for centuries.
BOOK_INTROS.Baruch: A short book attributed to Jeremiah's secretary Baruch, with prayers of confession, a meditation on wisdom, and a poem of comfort to Jerusalem. Includes the Letter of Jeremiah as chapter 6, in the arrangement of the 1611 King James Bible.
BOOK_INTROS.The Song of the Three Holy Children: An expansion within Daniel 3, containing the prayer of Azariah and the song the three young men sang as they walked unhurt in the fiery furnace.
BOOK_INTROS.Susanna: A short story of false accusation and rescue: a virtuous woman is saved from execution by the wisdom of the young Daniel.
BOOK_INTROS.Bel and the Dragon: Two short tales placed at the end of Daniel: Daniel exposes a fraudulent priesthood and slays a serpent worshipped as a god.
BOOK_INTROS.Prayer of Manasseh: A brief, beautiful prayer of repentance attributed to King Manasseh of Judah during his Babylonian captivity. Used in Christian liturgies for centuries.
BOOK_INTROS.1 Maccabees: The history of the Jewish revolt against Greek persecution under Antiochus IV, the rise of the Maccabean family, and the rededication of the Temple commemorated by Hanukkah.
BOOK_INTROS.2 Maccabees: An independent account of much of the same period as 1 Maccabees, with particular attention to martyrdom, prayer for the dead, and the Temple.
BOOK_INTROS.Matthew: The first Gospel, written with Jewish readers in mind, presenting Jesus as the long-awaited Messiah and teacher.
BOOK_INTROS.Mark: The shortest and most action-driven Gospel, emphasizing the works of Jesus and the call to follow.
BOOK_INTROS.Luke: A careful, orderly account of the life of Jesus, written by a physician with attention to outsiders, women, and the poor.
BOOK_INTROS.John: A theological reflection on the life of Jesus that opens with one of the most famous prologues in literature.
BOOK_INTROS.Acts: The story of how the message of Jesus spread from Jerusalem to Rome through the early church.
BOOK_INTROS.Romans: Paul's most systematic letter, exploring the gospel, justification, and the life of faith.
BOOK_INTROS.1 Corinthians: Paul addresses divisions, ethics, worship, and the resurrection in a young, troubled church.
BOOK_INTROS.2 Corinthians: A deeply personal letter in which Paul defends his ministry and writes about weakness and grace.
BOOK_INTROS.Galatians: A passionate defense of the gospel of grace against those who would add law to faith.
BOOK_INTROS.Ephesians: A letter on the cosmic scope of Christ's work and the unity of the church.
BOOK_INTROS.Philippians: Paul's joyful letter from prison to a beloved congregation.
BOOK_INTROS.Colossians: A short letter exalting Christ over every spiritual power and philosophy.
BOOK_INTROS.1 Thessalonians: Encouragement for a young church facing persecution and questions about Christ's return.
BOOK_INTROS.2 Thessalonians: A follow-up letter clarifying questions about the day of the Lord.
BOOK_INTROS.1 Timothy: Pastoral instructions to a younger leader on church life and leadership.
BOOK_INTROS.2 Timothy: Paul's last letter, written from prison, to his protégé Timothy.
BOOK_INTROS.Titus: A short letter on church leadership and Christian conduct.
BOOK_INTROS.Philemon: A personal letter asking a slave-owner to receive a runaway slave back as a brother.
BOOK_INTROS.Hebrews: A sustained meditation on Christ as the great high priest, written for believers tempted to give up.
BOOK_INTROS.James: Practical wisdom on faith, speech, wealth, and patience.
BOOK_INTROS.1 Peter: A letter of hope to scattered Christians facing suffering.
BOOK_INTROS.2 Peter: A letter warning against false teachers and reaffirming Christ's return.
BOOK_INTROS.1 John: A pastoral letter on the marks of true Christian life: love, truth, and assurance.
BOOK_INTROS.2 John: A short letter urging walking in truth and love.
BOOK_INTROS.3 John: A short personal letter about hospitality and church conflict.
BOOK_INTROS.Jude: A brief, fiery letter warning against false teachers.
BOOK_INTROS.Revelation: John's apocalyptic vision of Christ, the church, and the final renewal of all things.

BOOK_PITCHES.Matthew: The life of Jesus as told by a tax collector. Written to show Jesus as the fulfillment of Jewish prophecy.
BOOK_PITCHES.Mark: The shortest gospel. Fast, urgent, action-driven. Starts with Jesus already an adult. No birth story.
BOOK_PITCHES.Luke: Written by a doctor who interviewed eyewitnesses. The most detailed account, especially about women and outsiders.
BOOK_PITCHES.John: The most reflective gospel. Written decades after the others by someone who was there. Philosophical and personal.
BOOK_PITCHES.Genesis: The beginning of everything. Creation, Adam and Eve, the flood, Abraham. The origin story.
BOOK_PITCHES.Exodus: Escape from Egypt. Moses, the plagues, the Red Sea, the Ten Commandments.
BOOK_PITCHES.Numbers: Forty years wandering in the desert. Rebellion, faith, and survival between Egypt and the promised land.
BOOK_PITCHES.Joshua: Conquering the promised land. Military campaigns, land division, and a new beginning after Moses.
BOOK_PITCHES.Judges: Heroes and chaos. Before there were kings, there were judges, warriors and leaders in a lawless era.
BOOK_PITCHES.Ruth: A love story about loyalty, immigration, and belonging. One of the shortest books in the Bible.
BOOK_PITCHES.1 Samuel: The first king of Israel. Samuel, Saul, and the young David, including the fight with Goliath.
BOOK_PITCHES.2 Samuel: David's rise to power and his fall. War, betrayal, adultery, and the cost of being king.
BOOK_PITCHES.1 Kings: Solomon builds the temple, then the kingdom splits in two. Elijah appears as a prophet.
BOOK_PITCHES.2 Kings: Both kingdoms collapse. Elisha performs miracles. Israel and Judah are conquered and exiled.
BOOK_PITCHES.1 Chronicles: Israel's history retold from Adam to David. Genealogies and a second perspective on familiar events.
BOOK_PITCHES.2 Chronicles: Judah's history from Solomon to the exile. The temple, the kings, the fall of Jerusalem.
BOOK_PITCHES.Ezra: Returning from exile. The Jewish people rebuild their temple and their identity after Babylon.
BOOK_PITCHES.Nehemiah: Rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem. Leadership, opposition, and community restoration.
BOOK_PITCHES.Esther: A Jewish queen in Persia saves her people from genocide. God is never mentioned by name.
BOOK_PITCHES.Jonah: A prophet runs from God, gets swallowed by a fish, and learns about mercy. Stranger than you think.
BOOK_PITCHES.Acts: What happened after Jesus left. The early church, Paul's travels, and the spread of Christianity across the Roman Empire.
BOOK_PITCHES.Tobit: An angel in disguise, a magic fish, and a family reunion. Adventure and faith.
BOOK_PITCHES.Judith: A widow infiltrates an enemy camp and kills their general. One of the Bible's most dramatic heroines.
BOOK_PITCHES.1 Maccabees: War for independence. A family leads a revolt against a king who outlawed their religion.
BOOK_PITCHES.2 Maccabees: The same war told differently, more theological, more focused on martyrdom and miracle.
BOOK_PITCHES.1 Esdras: An alternate account of the temple rebuilding. Overlaps with Ezra and Chronicles.
BOOK_PITCHES.2 Esdras: Apocalyptic visions. Ezra asks God why the world is so unjust. God answers, sort of.
BOOK_PITCHES.Psalms: 150 songs and prayers. Joy, rage, grief, praise, the full range of human emotion directed at God.
BOOK_PITCHES.Song of Solomon: Erotic love poetry in the middle of the Bible. Yes, really. Beautiful, surprising, and ancient.
BOOK_PITCHES.Lamentations: Five poems of grief over the destruction of Jerusalem. Raw, structured, and devastating.
BOOK_PITCHES.Job: Why do good people suffer? A man loses everything and demands answers from God. God eventually responds, but not the way anyone expects.
BOOK_PITCHES.Proverbs: Practical advice about money, relationships, work, and character. One line at a time. Dip in anywhere.
BOOK_PITCHES.Ecclesiastes: Everything is meaningless. A wealthy king tries pleasure, work, and wisdom, and concludes none of it lasts.
BOOK_PITCHES.Leviticus: Religious law, sacrifice, purity, diet, festivals. The operating manual for ancient Israelite worship.
BOOK_PITCHES.Deuteronomy: Moses' farewell speech. He retells the law and the story so far before the people enter the promised land without him.
BOOK_PITCHES.Romans: Paul's masterwork. A systematic argument about sin, grace, faith, and freedom. The most influential letter in Christian history.
BOOK_PITCHES.1 Corinthians: A messy church in a wild city. Paul addresses divisions, lawsuits, sex, marriage, and the famous chapter on love.
BOOK_PITCHES.2 Corinthians: Paul defends his authority. The most personal and emotional of his letters. Weakness as strength.
BOOK_PITCHES.Galatians: Freedom vs rules. Paul argues that faith, not law-keeping, is what matters. A short, angry, important letter.
BOOK_PITCHES.Ephesians: Unity and identity. What does it mean to be part of the church? One of the most quoted letters.
BOOK_PITCHES.Philippians: Joy from prison. Paul writes to his favorite church from a jail cell. Warm, personal, and hopeful.
BOOK_PITCHES.Colossians: Who Jesus really is. A short letter about the supremacy of Christ over every power and philosophy.
BOOK_PITCHES.1 Thessalonians: What happens to people who die before Jesus returns? Paul's earliest letter, written to a worried church.
BOOK_PITCHES.2 Thessalonians: Waiting for the end. People quit their jobs because they thought Jesus was coming back immediately.
BOOK_PITCHES.1 Timothy: Advice to a young pastor. How to lead a church, handle false teaching, and live with integrity.
BOOK_PITCHES.2 Timothy: Paul's last letter. Written from prison, expecting execution. His final words to his closest student.
BOOK_PITCHES.Titus: Church leadership on the island of Crete. Practical instructions for building a healthy community.
BOOK_PITCHES.Philemon: A runaway slave meets Paul in prison. Paul sends him back with this letter asking his owner to free him.
BOOK_PITCHES.Hebrews: Old covenant vs new. A theological argument that Jesus fulfills and replaces the temple system. Author unknown.
BOOK_PITCHES.James: Faith without action is dead. Practical, blunt, and focused on how you actually live, not just what you believe.
BOOK_PITCHES.1 Peter: Suffering with hope. Written to persecuted Christians scattered across the Roman Empire.
BOOK_PITCHES.2 Peter: Warnings about false teachers and the end of the world. Peter's last word to the churches.
BOOK_PITCHES.1 John: God is love. A letter about truth, love, and how to tell real faith from false faith.
BOOK_PITCHES.2 John: A short note about truth and love. Thirteen verses. One page.
BOOK_PITCHES.3 John: A personal note about hospitality and a church leader who refuses to welcome visitors.
BOOK_PITCHES.Jude: Hold on to your faith. A short, fierce warning against people who distort the gospel.
BOOK_PITCHES.Revelation: The end of everything, and the beginning of something new. Visions, symbols, judgment, and a new heaven and earth.
BOOK_PITCHES.Isaiah: The biggest prophetic book. Judgment, comfort, and the most famous messianic prophecies. Two halves, two moods.
BOOK_PITCHES.Jeremiah: The weeping prophet. He warned Judah for forty years that destruction was coming. Nobody listened.
BOOK_PITCHES.Ezekiel: Bizarre visions. Wheels within wheels, a valley of dry bones, a rebuilt temple. Written in exile.
BOOK_PITCHES.Daniel: Dreams, a lion's den, and a fiery furnace. Half stories, half apocalyptic visions.
BOOK_PITCHES.Hosea: God tells a prophet to marry an unfaithful woman as a living metaphor for Israel's relationship with God.
BOOK_PITCHES.Joel: A plague of locusts becomes a vision of judgment and the outpouring of God's spirit.
BOOK_PITCHES.Amos: Justice for the poor. A farmer becomes a prophet and condemns the wealthy for exploiting the vulnerable.
BOOK_PITCHES.Obadiah: The shortest book in the Old Testament. One chapter against Edom for betraying their brother nation.
BOOK_PITCHES.Micah: Do justice, love mercy, walk humbly. A prophet challenges both the powerful and the complacent.
BOOK_PITCHES.Nahum: The fall of Nineveh. A vivid, poetic vision of an empire's collapse.
BOOK_PITCHES.Habakkuk: Why do you allow evil? A prophet argues with God about injustice. God answers but doesn't explain.
BOOK_PITCHES.Zephaniah: Judgment and restoration. The darkest warning followed by one of the most tender promises in scripture.
BOOK_PITCHES.Haggai: You've built nice houses for yourselves. When will you rebuild God's? A short, sharp challenge.
BOOK_PITCHES.Zechariah: Night visions about the future. Horses, lampstands, flying scrolls, and a coming king on a donkey.
BOOK_PITCHES.Malachi: The last prophet of the Old Testament. A dialogue between God and a people who've stopped caring.
BOOK_PITCHES.Susanna: A woman is falsely accused by two corrupt judges. Daniel exposes the lie. A courtroom drama.
BOOK_PITCHES.Bel and the Dragon: Daniel proves that idol worship is a fraud. Two stories about false gods, one funny, one deadly.
BOOK_PITCHES.Baruch: A letter from exile. Jeremiah's secretary writes to the people left in Jerusalem.
BOOK_PITCHES.Wisdom of Solomon: A meditation on justice, immortality, and why the righteous suffer. Philosophical and beautiful.
BOOK_PITCHES.Sirach: Ethics and everyday wisdom. How to handle money, friendship, speech, and death. The longest wisdom book.
